messages:
luis: FYI — customer reported a sudden invoice jump after a bunch of SSE disconnects. Dashboard shows ~240 tokens, invoice +1200 tokens. Can we take a look?
rebecca: rough timeframe/request id? any sample payloads or logs?
luis: Got a request id and the client side snippet. The client cancels mid-stream (ctrl-c) then reconnects. Curl SSE stream:```
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-large","stream":true,"prompt":"..."}' \n  https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate/sse
```
SSE observed events:```
data: {"delta":"Hello"}
data: {"delta":" world"}
event: partial_done
data: {"token_count":240}
event: client_cancel
// client reconnects and server emits final summary chunk
data: {"final_tokens":1200}
event: finalize
```
rebecca: ugh. do you also have server metering trace or billing rows?
luis: pasted server meter log (sanitized):```
[2065432109] req=rx-abc123 stream_start tokens=0
[2065432112] req=rx-abc123 chunk delta=2 tokens cumulative=240
[2065432116] req=rx-abc123 client_cancel status=499
[2065432120] req=rx-abc123 reconnect from same client, emitted final summary tokens=1200
[2065432125] billing: record emitted tokens=1200 for invoice batch 2026-03
```
ashok: thanks. this pattern rings a bell — we had a reconciliation edge where a reconnect + final summary chunk could be treated as an independent finalization and overwrite vs. dedupe the earlier partials. could be double counting of prefix vs final.
rebecca: can you attach request id and example invoice line? will need to open a billing investigation.
luis: request id rx-abc123. invoice line: `INV-2026-03: customer@example.com +1200 tokens`. Dashboard per-route shows only the live cumulative 240 tokens.
ashok: quick theory: when client cancels we emit a `client_cancel` event but the meter write is deferred. on reconnect we write a final summary without marking the previous partial writes as superseded. acceptance criteria: either we mark the earlier partials as stale or ensure final summary reconciles into the same aggregation key.
tom: if that is the bug, we should credit the customer immediately. Can you repro locally and drop a repro script? I'll queue a credit once confirmed. :+1: 
luis: repro steps I used:```bash
# open SSE stream, read 2 chunks then kill the client
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood-large","stream":true,"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate/sse &
PID=$!
sleep 1
kill -INT $PID  # simulate abrupt client cancel
# then open a new stream with same client id
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood-large","stream":true,"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate/sse
```
Observed: the billing table ended up with one row for 1200 tokens despite dashboard seeing the partial 240.
rebecca: sdk version? platform?
luis: SDK node v0.9.3, server runtime 1.14.2 (k8s), client is a web app using EventSource polyfill.
ashok: thanks. I can repro with that polyfill. creating a hotfix branch to change the meter write to include a reconciliation id (session + nonce) so final summary replaces partials. will put a canary on staging.
ashok: action items: (1) engineering hotfix PR, (2) support: propose temporary credit and inform customer, (3) billing: run backfill to dedupe already-invoiced duplicates.
rebecca: @tom can you prep the credit? please reference rx-abc123 + INV-2026-03.
tom: will do. creating billing ticket BT-4321 and provisional credit of 1200 tokens applied; need Eng signoff before forced backfill.
luis: customer notified and appreciates quick follow-up. they asked if this could recur.
ashok: won't recur once fix merged, but we'll monitor. adding a sanity alert on stream-reconcile failures.
billing-bot: [auto] BT-4321 created for INV-2026-03, provisional credit applied. Assigned: tom.
tom: closing loop — provisional credit in place, Eng to merge fix and we will run backfill if staging verifies.
rebecca: thanks team. leaving this thread open until fix in prod. :slightly_smiling_face:
